items.item: (e) E2: each moved section's title agrees with its target (or is untitled)
items.evidence:
All 182 moved sections agree with their target lot.

The question was what "target" means in the bar. Rule step 3 of decision.md defines Targets as "the carried lots of kind Lot with a non-blank carried number", and the bar's "its target" uses that defined term. Error risk defines a wrong remap as "one printed number naming different lots in two notices of one procedure". JUDGE checked the verifier's reading against both texts and adopts it. In 6876932, all 34 moved sections match the carried lot they join in number and title. "Produits surgelés" prints 3 in every notice of the chain and joins the carried lot that prints 3 "produits surgelés", so no number names two lots. The disagreement with the anchor's title comes from K1-refused notices: 21923843, 22231117 and 22219592 re-keyed the carry by today's positional merge at v4, v6 and v7, and rule step 5 leaves refused notices on today's fold by design. With the remap on, 0 keys are renumbered at v8; with it off, 17 are, and two numbers would each sit on two keys. Across all versions there are 75 per-key number changes with the remap against 82 without. No award moved, and the served head equals the remap-off head. check570.py's anchor-title reference is a proxy, valid only where no refused notice precedes the remapped one.

6298189/21804358 also agrees: its TED-MAIN_SITE "Lesná správa Zákamenné III" and its framework number match anchor LOT-11.
